beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twenty-three times fourteen: the area of this rectangle. Champ, what do you get?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Easy! Twenty times ten is two hundred. Three times four is twelve. So two hundred twelve!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Quick, and tidy. But let's break this rectangle apart by place value, and see if anything is missing.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twenty-three is twenty and three, so the long side splits right there.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fourteen is ten and four. Cut the tall side there too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now the big rectangle is four smaller ones, and each is easy to work out.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Mine are these two corners: twenty by ten, and three by four!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two hundred, and twelve. But look. Two pieces are still dark, and nobody counted them.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This one is twenty across and four down: eighty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And this one is three across and ten down: thirty.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Whoa. I forgot a hundred and ten!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So add every piece back. Two hundred, eighty, thirty, twelve.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three hundred twenty-two. Champ's two corners were only part of the rectangle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now the same idea with one digit on top: seven times three hundred forty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cut it by place: three hundreds, four tens, six ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: I squeezed the hundreds a little, so it fits on the screen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven times three hundred is two thousand one hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven times forty is two hundred eighty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And seven times six is forty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add the three pieces back: two thousand, four hundred twenty-two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three pieces, three easy products, one sum!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is one with a zero hiding in the middle: four times two thousand fifty-eight.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: There are no hundreds, so I can skip that part!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Don't skip it. Cut the strip by place: two thousand, no hundreds, fifty, eight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The hundreds piece has no width, only a sliver of nothing. It still sits in its place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four times two thousand is eight thousand. Four times zero is zero. Four times fifty is two hundred. Four times eight is thirty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add: eight thousand, plus nothing, plus two hundred, plus thirty-two. Eight thousand, two hundred thirty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six times forty-seven. Careful with the four in forty-seven. It is not four. It is forty.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So six times four is twenty-four, and six times seven is forty-two. Sixty-six!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's see what that four really is. Forty is four tens: four columns, each one ten wide.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each column is six tall and ten wide. Sixty, sixty, sixty, sixty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four sixties make two hundred forty. So six times forty is two hundred forty, never six times four. That twenty-four was twenty-four tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then the ones: six times seven is forty-two. Two hundred forty plus forty-two is two hundred eighty-two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So the tens piece is six times forty. Every digit keeps its place value.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Twelve times twelve? That one I just know. A hundred forty-four!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: You do, and it is a good fact to own. Here is why it is true: a square, twelve by twelve.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each twelve is a ten and a two. Cut both sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten by ten is one hundred. Ten by two is twenty. Two by ten is twenty again. Two by two is four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A hundred, twenty, twenty, four: one hundred forty-four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every fact up to twelve times twelve hides a picture like this one. If a fact slips away, split the twelve.

do.text: A fact slips away? Split the 12.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seven times twelve? Seven tens is seventy, seven twos is fourteen. Eighty-four!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One more job: checking. Someone says three times two hundred seventy-six is six hundred twenty-eight. True, or false?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Don't argue with it. Build it, one place at a time: two hundred, seventy, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three times two hundred is six hundred. Three times seventy is two hundred ten. Three times six is eighteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six hundred, plus two hundred ten, plus eighteen: eight hundred twenty-eight.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So it's false! Six twenty-eight is two hundred short.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Look at the middle piece. Two hundred ten holds two whole hundreds. Whoever dropped them wrote ten, and got six hundred twenty-eight. Every piece counts, carries and all.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to our rectangle. Where did the eighty come from?

do.text: Where does a piece come from?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every piece takes one number from the top and one from the side. This one: twenty across, and four down.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: And the thirty is three across and ten down!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four pieces, four pairs of sides. Nothing left out, nothing counted twice. Add them: three hundred twenty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Split by place. Multiply every piece. Add them all.
